newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil regional court grants 28.9 pct wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil regional court grants 28.9 pct wage hike.

text.p: A regional Brazilian court has followed a precedent set by the country's highest tribunal and granted 10,000 public sector workers a 28.9 percent wage hike, a court spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman for the Regional Federal Tribunal in Brasilia said its judges decided Tuesday to rule in favor of a claim lodged by a union representing current and retired employees of the social security services.
The ruling follows last month's decision by the country's supreme court, the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), to grant the 28.9 percent wage rise to 11 civil servants.
The 11 claimed that they were entitled to a pay rise given to military officers in 1993.
The government says it has no idea what the final cost of the STF decision might be to the public purse.
But independent analysts say that if extended to all the public sector, Brasilia may have to cough up $20 billion in backdated pay and $4.0 billion a year in extra payroll.
Several regional courts have already followed the precedent set by the STF. Their rulings can be challenged in the STF.
